summary: A live esports broadcast needs a director who chooses which camera goes on air and a caster who talks over that choice, every second and without knowing what comes next. Streaming video language models have learned to commentate, but only over a broadcast that a human director has already produced.
takeaways: We study live broadcast production, in which a model receives the raw camera of every player and must both direct and commentate from the past alone.
Streaming video language models have learned to commentate, but only over a broadcast that a human director has already produced.
We present DirCast, a single streaming video language model that does both.
